predicted_errors.error_location: Section 2.1 definition of Cal_T^D; Lemma 2.2; Appendix B proof; Appendix C Eq. (6) and subsequent theorem proofs
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Section 2.1 defines calibration with a 1/T factor: Cal_T^D = sum_p ((1/T) sum_t x_t(p)) D(nu_p,p). But Lemma 2.2 asserts this quantity equals FullSwapReg_T, whose definition is an unnormalized sum over T rounds. The Appendix B derivation obtains the unnormalized quantity sum_p sum_t x_t(p) D_R(nu_p|p), not the Section 2.1 definition. Likewise Eq. (6), Claim C.3, and the proof of Theorem 3.1 treat Cal_T as unnormalized. Thus Lemma 2.2 is off by a factor T under the paper's stated definition, and the main theorem bounds are not consistently expressed.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 2.3 definition of Bregman divergence and Lemma 2.1 / Appendix B
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The displayed definition is D_R(y||p) = R(p)-R(y)-<nabla R(y),p-y>, i.e. the Bregman divergence with gradient at y. However, Lemma 2.1 claims that its expectation is minimized at p=E[y], which is generally false for that orientation. The proof instead silently uses D_R(y||p)=R(y)-R(p)-<nabla R(p),y-p>, the reverse orientation, as shown by its first line: E[D_R(y||p)] = E[R(y)-R(p)-<nabla R(p),y-p>]. The strong-convexity assertion D_R(y||p) >= alpha||y-p||^2 and the proper-scoring-rule reduction also require the latter orientation. The stated divergence, proofs, and subsequent loss construction are therefore mutually inconsistent.

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The abstract claims that simplex l1 calibration is obtained after T=exp(O(log d/epsilon))=d^{O(1/epsilon)} rounds. The paper's stated general norm-calibration result, Theorem 1.1 / Corollary C.5, instead has exponent O(Rate(P,||.||)/epsilon^2); with negative entropy this gives at best the paper's own Section 1.1 claim d^{O(1/epsilon^2)} (and the displayed base also carries epsilon dependence). predicted_errors.error_location: Abstract and Section 1.1 discussion surrounding Theorem 1.4
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The abstract says the lower bound proves T >= exp(Omega(1/epsilon)), that it is tight up to constant factors in the exponent, and that it matches the upper bound. The actual final lower-bound statement, Theorem 4.3, only rules out T <= exp(c min{d^{1/7},epsilon^{-1/6}}). For sufficiently large d this yields only an exp(Omega(epsilon^{-1/6})) lower bound, not exp(Omega(1/epsilon)). It therefore cannot be tight against either the abstract's claimed exp(O(log d/epsilon)) upper bound or the theorem's epsilon-squared upper-bound dependence.

The informal Theorem 1.4 states the lower-bound horizon as exp(c min{d^{1/14},epsilon^{-1/6}}), whereas the formal Theorem 4.3 states exp(c min{d^{1/7},epsilon^{-1/6}}). These are materially different dimension dependences, and the proof of Theorem 4.3 uses d' approximately d/2 together with Theorem 4.1's d'^{1/14}, which supports the 1/14 exponent rather than the formal theorem's 1/7 exponent.

predicted_errors.error_location: Lemma 4.2 statement and proof; proof of Theorem 4.3
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Lemma 4.2 states a regret bound with factor diam_{||.||}(P'), but its proof applies Holder's inequality as ||nu_p-p|| · ||BR(p)-pi(BR(p))||_* and therefore proves a factor diam_{||.||_*}(P'), not the stated primal-norm diameter. The proof of Theorem 4.3 relies on this dual interpretation by taking P'=[-1,1]^{d'} and asserting an l_infinity diameter. Moreover, under the ordinary definition of diameter, [-1,1]^{d'} has l_infinity diameter 2, not 1. The stated lemma and its application do not match.
